_note: The end-to-end verification session reported in the dissertation's worked example. Recorded from a full pipeline run against a synthetic candidate with live model calls at every stage. This file is the single source for these figures; the dissertation reads from it rather than restating them inline.

candidate.profile: Synthetic backend engineer, four years of Python experience

skill_graph.note: Both absent skills were promoted to high-priority interview topics, and the flattening step moved the Kubernetes question ahead of questions about skills already evidenced.

observations: Greeting and sign-off were classified as logistics and excluded from scoring, so they did not dilute the average.

The candidate's admission that they had not used Kubernetes scored 50 rather than zero, because the rubric credits accuracy separately from completeness and an honest acknowledgement of a gap contains nothing incorrect.
That same answer carried the widest judge disagreement of the session at 10 points - the only moderate-consistency score in the interview, on the only genuinely partial answer.
